seat.description: The seat letter you were given, e.g. "B".

verdict.description: pass = meets the bar as is. conditional = meets it once your blockers are fixed. fail = the approach itself falls short of the bar.

summary.description: Two or three plain-English sentences: your overall judgement and the single most important reason.

scores.description: One entry per scorecard criterion in the brief, in the same order.

score.description: 1 to 10. 7 means meets the bar; below 7 means it does not.

blockers.description: Problems YOU raise that must be fixed before this meets the bar. Not nitpicks. In later rounds, repeat each of your own earlier blockers with its current status.

id.description: Your seat letter plus a number, e.g. "B2". Keep the same id across rounds.

claim.description: What is wrong and what it would cause, in one or two sentences.

evidence.description: What proves it: a file and line, a quoted passage, a command you ran and its output, a source URL. Empty string if you have none.

checked.description: true only if you personally looked at the evidence in this run (read the file, ran the command, opened the page). false if it is reasoning or memory.

fix.description: The smallest change that would remove the blocker.

status.description: new in round 1. Later: held, or withdrawn (then position_changes must say what convinced you).

responses.description: Round 1: empty. Later rounds: one entry for every blocker raised by OTHER seats in the dossier.

steelman.description: The strongest honest version of that blocker, in one sentence, before you judge it.

stance.description: Debate rounds: agree, dispute or unsure. Resubmissions: fixed, not_fixed, or fixed_new_problem (the fix caused a new problem; explain it in evidence).

evidence.description: What you checked that supports your stance. A dispute with no evidence counts as unsure.

position_changes.description: Every place where your verdict, a score, or one of your blockers changed since your last round. Empty in round 1.

convinced_by.description: Quote the specific evidence or argument that changed your mind. Agreement with the majority is not a reason.

open_questions.description: Things only the owner can answer that would change your verdict. Keep it short.
